clue.text: How's your father's odd little dog with exchange of PM?

indicators.note: swapping a P and an M between the two words means their letters are rearranged

parts.note: rummy is British slang for odd or strange
a puppy is a young, little dog

explanation.surface: A question about whether somebody's father owns a strange little dog that swapped places with the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMMY PUPPY becomes the answer when one M and one P trade places, so the 'exchange of PM' is a disguised anagram; 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are jokey British euphemisms for sexual intercourse, the first a coy music-hall phrase.

clue.text: Apply to God — put in heater to apply paint

indicators.note: put in tells us one group of letters goes inside the word for heater

parts.note: the sun is what heats the Earth
to apply to someone is to ask them, as one may pray to a god
G is a standard abbreviation for God

explanation.surface: A slightly mystical instruction to pray, then warm up, before painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places the prayer and G inside the heater; the definition reads as a tool used to apply paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray gun is a tool that atomises paint, so it is a device for applying it.

clue.text: Wanting too much colour to catch editor

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: grey is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone describes a colour as clutching at an editor, in an overreaching way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being greedy is wanting more than one needs or deserves, an adjective-for-phrase synonym.

clue.text: See 22 across
Make a single purchase, then liberate a person

definitions.meaning: the shop slogan 'buy one, ...' completes with the answer: after a single purchase comes a second item gratis
to secure somebody's release is to have them set at liberty

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a completion: 'buy one' is the single purchase, and the familiar retail offer follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The supermarket offer gives a second item gratis, and literally the words mean to secure one person's release.

clue.text: More than a hundred worthy fellows with energy say we shall

parts.note: over means more than

OM is the Order of Merit, an honour held by distinguished people
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that more than a hundred worthy men, with energy, will prevail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a completion: 'We Shall ...' is the civil rights anthem, and 'say' signals the phrase is quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: The protest song title We Shall Overcome supplies the missing word after these two.

clue.text: Crippled by guilt, cease to be a water regulator

indicators.note: being crippled means being broken and twisted out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone so paralysed by guilt that they stop functioning as a water regulator.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluicegate is a sliding gate that controls the flow of water in a channel.

clue.text: See 7
Better example for capital

parts.note: upper means superior or better, as in upper class
a case is an instance or example

explanation.surface: A better instance of what makes a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are called upper case, after the printer's top type tray.

clue.text: Lines coming in through house

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: via means by way of, through
L is an abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Lines of people entering by way of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or seaside house.

clue.text: Vegetable cooked on ice with some nettles for me, as 22 23 4 said

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: cooked here means doctored or rearranged, as in cooking the books
only some of the word for nettles is wanted, so its end is cut away

parts.note: Urtica is the botanical genus of nettles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for a pea dish on ice with nettles, apparently quoting a historical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: URTICA loses CA to give URTI; ON ICE becomes CEINO. The definition refers to the linked answer at 22, 23 and 4, the Prime Minister who returned from Munich in 1938.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain famously declared in 1938 that his deal with Hitler had brought this, a phrase now ironic.

clue.text: See 11
Very small beast — I am surprised

parts.note: a pig is a beast
'my!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a tiny animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigmy, a variant of pygmy, is used adjectivally for something unusually small.

clue.text: They happen to female getting round males in US state

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania
a hen is a female bird
O is round in shape
men are males

explanation.surface: Something about a woman surrounding men in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are events or occurrences, things that take place.

clue.text: Old sculptor's realisation of theory outside the box

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: praxis is practice as opposed to theory, putting ideas into action
the box is British slang for television, the tele

explanation.surface: A sculptor of old making his theory real by thinking outside the box.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. 'Outside the box' reads as the cliché about original thinking, but it is a container instruction; 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxiteles was a celebrated Athenian sculptor of the fourth century BC.

clue.text: Hate figure's old old shirt mended

parts.note: antic is an archaic form of antique, meaning very old

indicators.note: mended means repaired or put back together, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A villain's ancient shirt has been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mended' rearranges SHIRT into HRIST. The 's is 'is'; ANTIC for 'old' leans on its archaic sense of antique, which the blog commenters thought shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antichrist is the great adversary of Christ in Christian scripture, a figure of loathing.

clue.text: Reach, for example, improperly into title deed that was signed by 22 23 4 …

indicators.note: into places the scrambled letters inside the word for title deed

parts.note: a muniment is a document such as a title deed proving rights
EG abbreviates the Latin exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone improperly inserts a reach into a title deed that a famous politician signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach' poses as a verb but is anagram fodder for 'improperly'; 'into' sets the result inside a rare legal word for a title deed. The pact is the 1938 Munich deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain signed the 1938 pact with Hitler, Mussolini and Daladier ceding the Sudetenland.

clue.text: Eliminate desire to see who's who dramatically

parts.note: to cast out or cast off is to get rid of
list is an archaic word for desire or wish

explanation.surface: Throwing off longing in order to learn who someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast list names who plays whom in a theatrical production.

clue.text: Got title, none other, and was hurt

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters take a different form

parts.note: bled means suffered a wound

explanation.surface: Someone received a peerage, unlike anyone else, and suffered for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be raised to the nobility, receiving a title.

clue.text: … (where's Halifax?) — in the past — shirk problem

indicators.note: in means the reshaped letters go inside the word for the past

parts.note: yore means time long gone, as in days of yore

indicators.note: a problem leaves letters in disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a reflection on where Halifax lies and dodging problems long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 16. 'problem' rearranges SHIRK into RKSHI. Halifax is a West Yorkshire town, and also the name of Chamberlain's Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Halifax is a town in the county of Yorkshire in northern England, so the county answers the question.

explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is a deep narrow valley, a synonym of gorge.

clue.text: Hardbitten type fits into diplomacy nicely

indicators.note: fits into means the word lies within the following words

explanation.surface: A hardened sort neatly slotting into the world of diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic distrusts others' motives, a hardened, world-weary person.

clue.text: Animals covering islands formed from land …

parts.note: a coat is a covering, as of paint

explanation.surface: Animals that cover islands, made from some land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed from land …' gives a second route with 22: the letters of SCOTIA rearranged, the land following NOVA, where Halifax is the capital.

Head and shoulders cover

a sleeveless garment worn over the shoulders
